title: How a CPU Executes Instructions
description: What the hardware does with the bytes the ISA course decoded: dependencies, execution width, branch prediction and speculation -- measured with an instrument that was validated before it was trusted.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Read all 6 concepts, reproduce the 37 measured checks in courses/exe/assets/samples/crosscheck.py, and add a measurement of your own that survives the noise floor

concepts.title: Measure the Instrument First
concepts.description: A TSC tick is not a cycle, the fences are not optional, and the noise floor decides what may be claimed.

concepts.title: Latency and Throughput
concepts.description: A dependent chain costs 2.7x an independent operation, and the ratio is the execution width made visible.

concepts.title: A Dependency Is a Constraint, Not a Cost
concepts.description: What a loop-carried chain is, why the loop hid the first measurement, and how far an address constrains the front end.

concepts.title: The Front End and the Branch Predictor
concepts.description: A branch whose direction repeats with period 1, 4, 16 or 64 costs the same as one that is never taken.

concepts.title: Speculation, and What Could Not Be Measured
concepts.description: No mispredict penalty was observed at any pattern period, and without a PMU that is a limit rather than a result.

concepts.title: The Instrument and the Oracle Loop
concepts.description: What the harness asserts, why it asserts shapes rather than values, and how to break a checker on purpose.
